In the combined cycle, a heat recovery steam generator (HRSG) extracts heat from the CT exhaust to power a steam turbine. The IGCC CO capture cases consume more extraction steam than the non-capture cases, thus 2 reducing the steam turbine output. In addition, the capture cases have a higher auxiliary load requirement than non-capture cases, which serves to further reduce net plant output. While the two CTs provide 464 MW gross output in all IGCC cases, the overall combined cycle gross output ranges 685–765 MW, which results in a range of net output from 499 (Case B5B-Q) to 641 MW (Case B4A). The coal feed rate required to achieve the gross power output is also different between the six cases, ranging 197,500–219,000 kg/hr (435,400–482,900 lb/hr). The NGCC cases also have different gross and net power outputs because of the CT size constraint. The state-of-the-art 2017 F-class CT used to model the NGCC cases comes in a standard size of 238 MW when operated at conditions set by ISO. Each case uses two CTs for a combined gross output of 477 MW. In the combined cycle, a HRSG extracts heat from the CT exhaust to power a steam turbine. The state-of-the-art 2017 H-class CT comes in a standard size of 343 MW when operated at conditions set by ISO. Each case uses two CTs for a combined gross output of 686 MW. In the combined cycle, an HRSG extracts heat from the CT exhaust to power a steam turbine. The net output in the NGCC CO capture case is significantly reduced compared to the non- 2 capture case due to the high auxiliary power load and significant extraction steam requirement of the CO capture system. 2 While the two F-frame CTs provide 477 MW gross output, the overall combined cycle gross output ranges 690–740 MW, which results in a range of net output from 640 MW (Case B31B.95) to 727 MW (Case B31A). The natural gas feed rate is the same in both cases at 93,272 kg/hr (205,630 lb/hr). While the two H-class CTs provide 686 MW gross output, the overall combined cycle gross output ranges 942–1,009 MW, which results in a range of net output from 877 MW (Case B32B.95) to 992 MW (Case B32A).
